``` ## Data: aggregating trial responses {#preparing-simple-span-data .m3-model-slide} ::: {.m3-preparation-content} ```{.r} simple_span <- trials |> summarise(corr = sum(response_type == "correct"), other = sum(response_type == "other"), npl = sum(response_type == "npl"), .by = c(id, exp, setsize, n_corr, n_other, n_npl)) ``` ```{.text} id exp setsize n_corr n_other n_npl corr other npl 1 10_openset openset 2 1 0 1 23 0 0 2 10_openset openset 2 1 1 0 23 0 0 3 10_openset openset 2 1 1 2 23 0 0 ``` ::: ## Specify: the simple-span model {#specify-categories-and-their-option-counts .smaller .m3-model-slide auto-animate=true} ::::: {.m3-model-content} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="1-6|2|3|4|5"} model_simple <- m3( resp_cats = c("corr", "other", "npl"), num_options = c("n_corr", "n_other", "n_npl"), version = "ss", choice_rule = "softmax" ) ``` ::: ```{=html} ``` :::: {.m3-model-explanations} ::: {.fragment .current-visible fragment-index=0} `resp_cats`: observed response counts for Correct, Others, and NPL. ::: ::: {.fragment .current-visible fragment-index=1} `num_options`: available options in the same category order. ::: ::: {.fragment .current-visible fragment-index=2} `version`: `"ss"` = simple span · `"cs"` = complex span · `"custom"` = custom model. ::: ::: {.m3-choice-stage .fragment .current-visible fragment-index=3} `choice_rule`: `"simple"` = Luce’s choice rule · `"softmax"` = exponential choice weights. :::: {.columns .m3-choice-comparison} ::: {.column .m3-choice-panel} ::: {.m3-choice-equation} $$ P(k)=\frac{n_k A_k}{\sum_j n_j A_j} $$ ::: ::: ::: {.column .m3-choice-panel} ::: {.m3-choice-equation} $$ P(k)=\frac{n_k\exp(A_k)}{\sum_j n_j\exp(A_j)} $$ ::: ::: :::: ::: :::: ::::: ## Specify: parameter formulas {#specify-how-do-a-and-c-vary .smaller} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="true"} formula_simple <- bmf( c ~ 0 + ss_fac + (0 + ss_fac | id), a ~ 0 + ss_fac + (0 + ss_fac | id) ) ``` ::: ::: {.incremental} - `0 + ss_fac`: a separate mean for each **set size**. - `(0 + ss_fac | id)`: correlated participant deviations at each set size. ::: ## Fit: the simple-span model {#fit-once-load-the-result-for-the-workshop .smaller .m3-model-slide} ::::: {.m3-model-content} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="2-5"} fit_simple <- bmm( formula = formula_simple, model = model_simple, data = dat_simple, prior = priors_simple, chains = 4, cores = 4, iter = 5000, warmup = 2000, control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95), sample_prior = "yes", backend = "cmdstanr", seed = 2026, file = here("models", "m3_simple"), file_refit = "on_change" ) ``` ::: The sampling arguments work the same way as in the SDT model. ::::: ## Evaluate: observed and predicted responses {#evaluate-does-m3-reproduce-the-responses .smaller .m3-figure} `posterior_epred(fit_simple)` predicts counts in **all three categories**. Predictions match the observed proportions for correct responses and both error types. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](../data/figures/m3_simple_predictive.png){fig-alt='Observed and predicted open-set response proportions, with participant-level standard errors, across three categories.' width=100%} ::: ::: ## Evaluate: item and binding estimates {#interpret-item-memory-and-binding-memory .smaller .m3-figure} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](../data/figures/m3_simple_parameters.png){fig-alt='Open-set item and binding memory medians and 95 percent credible intervals across set sizes, in blue and orange facets on a 0 to 6 activation scale.' width=90%} ::: ::: - Item memory tends to decline with set size, but the estimates are uncertain. - Binding memory declines clearly with set size. ## Extension: M3 for complex span {.section-divider} How does M3 account for distractor activation? ::: {.m3-slide-link} ```{=html} ``` ::: ## Task: complex span {#complex-span-instructions .m3-task-slide} ```{=html}

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
